description: Stati is a TypeScript-first static site generator. Write Markdown, template with Eta, and rebuild only what changed with Incremental Static Generation. Packages: @stati/core, @stati/cli, @stati/images and create-stati.
rules: Stati is a TypeScript-first static site generator. Packages: @stati/core (engine), @stati/cli (the stati command), create-stati (scaffolder), @stati/images (optional image provider).
Create a site with `npx create-stati my-site`, then `cd my-site` and `npm run dev`. Markdown pages live in site/, static assets in public/, and the output goes to dist/.
Configure in stati.config.ts (or stati.config.js) with defineConfig() from @stati/core. Prefer TypeScript examples over JavaScript.
Stati 2 removed stati.partials and eta.filters. Use stati.include('path', props) for components and the top-level `helpers` option, called as stati.helpers.name(value). See Upgrading to Stati 2.
Use stati.include(), stati.layout(), stati.body and stati.props in .eta templates. Eta's own include, includeAsync, layout, block and blockAsync are blocked.
Eta attributes cannot mix static text with a tag, as in class="a-<%= b %>". Make the whole value dynamic: a template literal, or stati.propValue('base', cond && 'active').
Pages are Markdown files with YAML front matter. site/blog/hello.md becomes /blog/hello. A .eta file is a layout, shell or include, never a page.
Incremental Static Generation caches in .stati/manifest.json. Clear it with `stati build --clean`, or selectively with `stati invalidate "tag:news"`, `"path:/blog/"` or `"age:3months"`.
Responsive images (images.responsive) and Open Graph cards (images.og) need the @stati/images package. Without it the build fails with an install message.
For Tailwind CSS, pass --tailwind-input and --tailwind-output to `stati dev` and `stati build`. Production builds link the stylesheet by its hashed file name.
Search, sitemap, robots.txt, RSS feeds and SEO meta tags are built in and configured in stati.config.ts. Enable search with search: { enabled: true }.
Requires Node.js 22.20+ or 24+. npm, pnpm, yarn and bun all work as package managers.
For concepts such as ISG, templates and routing, prefer the docs-site guides over package READMEs. For quickstart steps, prefer create-stati and @stati/cli docs.
